messages:
sasha: Quick notePTQ ensemble canary for 'raven-lite-int8' showing a parse failure spike. parse_failure_rate=2.1% vs baseline 0.3%. Samples look like wrong container types, e.g. `tool_call` sometimes an array, sometimes missing 'name'. Also sporadic trailing plaintext suffixes.

jamie: Is this from the onboard harness or the prod canary?

sasha: Onboard harness. Ran: `./canary/run_structured_eval --model raven-lite-int8 --variants ensemble,base --n 4000`. Logged fields: parse_failure_rate, schema_mismatch_entropy, funcall_omit_rate.

mike: Can you paste a redacted failing output? Tiny samples are most useful.

sasha: Example (redacted):
```
{"req_id":"abc","tool_call":[{"args":"{\"id\":\"u1\"}"}]}
```
Here `tool_call` should be an object like `{"name":...,"args":...}`.

oliver: Array vs object flip smells like streaming/ndjson concat from one quantized head. Any relation with batching or kv cache?

deepa: Telemetry: spike aligns with batch_size >= 8 and seq_len bucket > 512. Replay single-request often passes.

sasha: Proposed actions: 1) run param sweep batch_size=[1,2,4,8] x seq_len buckets and record token offsets; 2) enable strict-json-wrapper to capture raw token stream for failures; 3) temporarily turn off ensemble fallback on the canary.

jamie: I'll flip the routing flag off and add an alert if parse_failure_rate > 1% sustained 5m. @triage-bot create ticket if threshold hit.

triage-bot: Created INF-1429: "raven-lite-int8 PTQ ensemble parse spike" assigned to @sasha and @jamie, priority P2.

mike: Requesting logits + token boundary indices for 30 failures so we can inspect subtoken merge behavior at int8. Could be quantized head producing merged tokens with stray separators.

sasha: Added a repro gist and the sweep job: https://gist.github.com/sasha/raven-ptq-batch-sweep. Kicking off now and will paste 2 reproducible samples here when available.

jamie: If batch sensitivity reproduces, we can patch the canary autoscaler to cap batch_size for the model until we patch the ensemble gating. Also consider adding an output sanitizer to coerce `tool_call` containers into expected shape as a short-term mitigation.

oliver: Agree. For the sanitizer, prefer a non-destructive healer that logs both original and sanitized payload so we can trace regressions.

sasha: Will run sweep, collect token stream traces and dump. Will update this thread with artifacts and a minimal failing input for local repro. :thumbsup:
